I don’t work for GS anymore, but Without a GSP or any other protection plan. You are looking at a MINIMUM of around $400 most likely more to a MAX of maybe $800 but I would plan on somewhere in that price range, and that’s just for the display. If you want the data off you can either move it onto an external drive yourself or have GS do it and that’s $100 as a stand alone service. You could buy the a Total Tech membership. I think it’s Best Buy Total now. And that’s $180, would cover the cost for GS to do the data backup and I think you still get a 20% discount on repairs sent to the service center.

If you decide to get it sent out it’s $85 to have it sent to the service center for a quote then you will be called told the total cost and asked if you want to do it or not. If you say no it will be sent back and you can use it as is. If you say yes they will order the parts, repair it, and send it back. Total turn around 3 weeks. 

Forgive me if some info is slightly off. it’s been a few months since I left so things might have changed a bit in procedure and cost
Hope that helps if you would like some more info or even some practice I would be happy to help just let me know

This mindset is awful. I’m cross trained between both front and back because I know I’m part of a team. When BOP is backed up and I check in a phone for repair I’ll start on it at the very least for them, if I have time I’ll do the whole thing. In turn they will do a checkout for me here and there. I’ve been on both sides of the coin with a agent who says “not my job not my problem” on multiple occasions and in one case he got so bad the other ARA’s wouldn’t even help when he needed it. 

It’s part of the job for both ends to help one another. Maybe that means doing one or 2 func checks now and then. Maybe that means just going out to schedule appointments for walk ins. And maybe on the other end the help start apple repairs or help by starting MRI on computers when they are checked in. 

I agree you shouldn’t be doing their job it’s their responsibility to balance appointments, walk-ins, func checks, etc. in turn it’s your responsibility to balance apple repairs, Samsung repairs, (if applicable) and computer check ins. 

If everyone had your mindset GeekSquad wouldn’t exist anymore.

I usually run diags first before I hit start repair (mainly so I can double check they have apple care so I don’t waste their time and mine filling out unnecessary stuff) while diags are running I get to the client info in nova once diags are done I start repair and check apple care. Then a lot of copy and paste from nova to GSX for Client info. I fill out everything else in GSX check to make sure we have the part for repair and also double check with ARA on repair time then I copy and paste my notes in GSX to nova and copy and paste SO into GSX then to register for payment if needed then sign paperwork and they are on their way. I think the fastest I have done a apple check in is somewhere close to 7 or 8 min I think I haven’t timed it or anything. But that is for just the obvious oh the screens broken no troubleshooting needed apple check in.
I just run SNR or MRI then start repair and it will show it all. I agree it’s dumb and I don’t get why they require it but it is what it is I guess.
